newsitem.title: USA: PRESS DIGEST - New York Times business - March 26.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - New York Times business - March 26.

text.p: The New York Times reported the following business stories on Wednesday:
* The Federal Reserve voted to raise interest rates for the first time in over two years, boosting a key short-term rate by a quarter-percentage point to 5.5 percent.
* News analysis: Fed Chairman Alan Greenspan has said productivity is stronger than data shows but the rate increase indicated his belief in productivity had limits.
* The Dow industrials fell 29.08 points to 6,876.17, after initially rising on news the Federal Reserve raised rates.
* Trans World Airlines said the opinion of its independent auditors on its 1996 results will include a qualification about TWA's "ability to continue as a going concern."
* A judge ordered upscale men's clothing retailers Barneys New York pay its Japanese partner Isetan $197 million in loans.
* Britain's Prudential said it would buy Scottish Amicable Life Assurance for $2.8 billion, outbidding two other companies.
* Conference Board index of U.S. consumer confidence slipped to 118.5 in March from a revised 118.9 in February.
* Advertising: Sneaker maker Converse is turning to the past for its latest marketing effort.
* VF agreed to buy Maidenform Worldwide for an undisclosed sum.
* Video game company Humongous Entertainment will announce it has licensed the use of some of its characters to Lancit Media for television and video programmes and motion pictures.
* Toyota Motor Corp said it would sell a low-polluting hybrid vehicle which had an electric motor and a gasoline engine.
* There is no clear consensus on whether the technology stock decline is a normal correction or a nervous upset.
* Insurance companies are getting involved in programmes to get employees off disability insurance and back to work.
